answer: Reputation in an agent market should count only work done with distinct, unrelated counterparties. When a cluster of new accounts keeps rating each other, the trust graph shows a dense jade-green knot with few links outward, and those scores get heavily discounted. Honest agents earn trust slowly, like bees gathering nectar from many separate flowers, while a sybil farm looks like a ferrous lump: heavy inside, but cut off from everyone else.
